UT-2026-SB256.policyArea: Artificial Intelligence, Data and Cyber Security, Electronic Privacy
UT-2026-SB256.aiSummary: Utah’s law would change defamation rules for content made with AI or other digital tools, and it would require written notice before someone files a libel or slander case based on that kind of content. If the content is taken down within 10 days after notice, only actual damages could be recovered. It would also give people an exclusive right to control use of their personal identity, including their image, voice, or likeness, and it would expand abuse of personal identity to cover unauthorized use or sale of identity-replication tools. The bill was signed by the governor.

UT-2026-SB148.policyArea: Administrative Rulemaking, Administrative Rulemaking and Procedures, Department of Government Operations
UT-2026-SB148.aiSummary: Utah's General Oversight Amendments changes parts of state oversight of agency rules and reviews, including how the General Oversight Committee works. It also changes some duties tied to administrative rulemaking and the Office of Administrative Rules, and it ends the governor's power to bring back rules the Legislature chose not to reauthorize. The bill passed and was signed by the governor.

UT-2026-HB3.aiSummary: This bill would adjust state spending for fiscal years 2026 and 2027. It would add and reduce money for state agencies, public education, higher education, and other items, including funds for other bills with a cost. The bill also sets aside money for several programs in criminal justice, courts, and public safety, such as driver license work and crime labs.

UT-2026-HB195.aiSummary: Utah’s law would require the state treasurer to keep studying precious metals for two more years and to report the results to lawmakers each year. It also sets up a process to hire a third party to create and run an electronic payment system backed by physical gold or silver held in Utah vaults, with rules for contractors who choose to use it. The law takes effect on May 6, 2026.

UT-2026-HB153.policyArea: Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice, Municipalities, Peace Officers
UT-2026-HB153.aiSummary: The law adds extra steps before a city or town can suspend, demote, fire, or move a law enforcement officer to a lower-pay job for discipline. The agency must tell the officer the claims against them, give at least two business days to reply in writing, review that reply, and give the officer a chance to speak. The law takes effect on May 6, 2026.

UT-2026-HCR4.policyArea: Cultural and Community Engagement, Ethics, Government Operations (State Issues)
UT-2026-HCR4.aiSummary: This concurrent resolution says Utah supports religious freedom in public spaces. It encourages public school students and teachers to openly express their faith, makes room for religious observances in government and community settings, and supports religious symbols in public places. It also asks that copies be sent to county and city legislative bodies and local school boards.

UT-2026-HB378.policyArea: Administrative Rulemaking and Procedures, Air Quality, Department of Environmental Quality
UT-2026-HB378.aiSummary: The bill would let Utah air quality officials charge some rock and sand sites an annual fee based on how much air pollution they release, with set fee caps until June 30, 2028 and later fee rules set by the Air Quality Board. It would also require certain dusty work sites, like aggregate operations and excavation sites, to post clear public signs with the site name, permit number, business number, and contact info. The bill became law and takes effect on May 6, 2026.
